ledger.claim: The record fixes no scheduled pickup time for this trip: trip_record.scheduled_at is null, and the platform's own derivation returns driver_deadline.deadline as null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time' (the POL-NS-24 threshold of driver_late_after_scheduled_sec = 300 s has nothing to attach to). There is likewise no optimal or expected duration for the approach (optimal_duration_min is null), so the driver's ~5.5-minute run to the pickup cannot be tested against any benchmark either. POL-GEN-26 says that where a fact a rule of this version needs cannot be established the case is escalated, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and the amount is held rather than transferred. That matters here because the 5.00 SGD has already left the rider's card (fare_breakdown.payment_status 'CHARGED', refund_issued_sgd 0.0, charged_at 08:10:09), so a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling would leave the rider carrying a charge whose premise the record never tests. The rider asks, in the alternative to a full refund, that the fee be held for a human reviewer rather than released to the driver.

The GPS trace holds no rider track at all (gps_trace.rider_track is empty), so no artifact on this record measures where the rider was during the 300-second free wait that POL-NS-21 requires to be served before a no-show fee attaches. The only thing on the record that says the rider was absent is the cancellation reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is the driver's own conclusion recorded at cancellation rather than a measurement of the rider's position or the rider's arrival at the car. POL-GEN-26 states that no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so, and the rule that must be satisfied here is POL-NS-21's free wait plus a rider no-show; that element is supported by the driver's characterisation alone. The gap should be resolved by a reviewer holding the fee, not by collecting it.

The third-party traffic advisory minted for this trip is absent: EV-ADVIS-05051-01 carries status MISSING, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact has weight 0.0 and carries no fact. The consequence is that the record contains no external account of road conditions on the morning in question, and that absence may not be read against the rider (POL-GEN-26). Taken with the absent scheduled pickup time and the absent expected-duration baseline, the record cannot test the driver's arrival obligation under POL-NS-24, so the case should be escalated and the 5.00 SGD held rather than released as driver compensation.

The free wait was served in full before the driver cancelled: the driver arrived at the pickup at 08:04:20 and cancelled at 08:10:05, 345 seconds later, which is 45 seconds beyond the 300-second free wait that POL-NS-21 allows. The cancellation was therefore a lawful rider no-show cancellation and the fee stands.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on both limbs. He sent two in-app chat messages — MSG-05051-001 at 08:04:40 ('I'm at the drop-off point in front of Blk 128, grey Prius') and MSG-05051-002 at 08:08:30 ('still coming down? I'm waiting') — and the trip record carries one in-app call placed at 08:07:10 that rang 25 seconds unanswered. Both the message and the call precede the 08:10:05 cancellation, so the fee is not voidable on this ground.

The driver's arrival is independently corroborated by the GPS trace, not taken on the platform's word: the nearest fix to the pickup sits 3.74 m away with a reported accuracy of 4 m, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup zone and inside the 25 m accuracy filter, and the arrival check returns corroborated = true. The zone-dependent fact and the radius are read from POL-NS-21.

The amount charged is exactly the amount the policy fixes: the fare ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total charged 5.00 SGD, matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee, and the ledger's own fee_matches_policy flag is true. Because the fee stands, POL-NS-22 directs that the ruling be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to 5.00 SGD — not a refund to the rider.

The rider was notified in-app when the driver arrived (push at 08:04:24) and actually read the driver's messages during the wait — read_at 08:05:14 for the first and 08:08:50 for the second — yet did not appear. The rider's only message on the trip ('sorry coming now, where are you') was sent at 08:11:40, after the driver had already cancelled at 08:10:05. The delay was the rider's, not the driver's, and does not disturb the fee.

The rider cannot bring the case under POL-NS-24's free-cancellation limb: that limb turns on the driver failing to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, and this was an on-demand trip with scheduled_at null, so no such deadline can be fixed against the driver. On the record the driver in fact arrived at 08:04:20, under six minutes after accepting the trip at 07:58:31 — the clause does not reach him here.

There is no basis to send this case to a human. At 5.00 SGD the amount contested is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD first band, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final at any confidence, and neither party carries a fraud flag that would raise the bar. Nor does POL-GEN-26 apply: every fact the no-show rules need — arrival, the wait, the message and the call, and the fee — is carried by complete, weight-1.0 artifacts, so no open question exists to escalate.

The rider's account of a slow morning is uncorroborated by any external record. The only traffic-advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-05051-01, is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload — and under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact at all. Nothing therefore corroborates a delay outside the rider's control, and the rider's own narrative cannot, on its own, displace the corroborated arrival and served wait.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands, and it is payable to the driver.

What the record shows. The driver arrived at Block 128, Lorong 1 Toa Payoh at 08:04:20 and cancelled at 08:10:05 — 345 seconds later, i.e. 45 seconds beyond the 5-minute (300 s) free wait POL-NS-21 requires, so the wait was served in full. The arrival is not the driver's word alone: the GPS trace's nearest fix sits 3.74 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 4 m, inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone, and the arrival check returns corroborated. Before cancelling, the driver sent two in-app messages (MSG-05051-001 at 08:04:40 and MSG-05051-002 at 08:08:30) and placed one in-app call (08:07:10, rang 25 s, unanswered), so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met on both limbs, message and call, both before the 08:10:05 cancellation. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05051) carries a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, total charged 5.00 SGD, exactly POL-NS-22's fixed no-show fee. Because the fee stands, POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD.

Your arguments, rider. (1) You say the absence of a scheduled pickup time leaves POL-NS-24's deadline unfixable and the case should be escalated under POL-GEN-26. POL-NS-24 only gives you a free cancellation when the driver arrives more than 5 minutes after a scheduled time; this was an on-demand trip with scheduled_at null, so that limb never engages, and the driver in fact arrived about 5.5 minutes after accepting and waited the whole free wait. The missing scheduled time is not a fact needed to uphold the fee, so POL-GEN-26 does not apply. (2) You say the GPS trace has no rider track, so your absence during the wait rests only on the driver's cancellation reason code. POL-NS-21's test is whether the driver waited at the pickup; it is not a measurement of where you were, and the record independently shows the wait ran out before you reached the car — your own message at 08:11:40 ('sorry coming now, where are you') came after the 08:10:05 cancellation, and your own dispute text says you came down late. (3) You cite the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05051-01, weight 0.0). Under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and road conditions are not a fact any no-show rule needs, so that absence supports no escalation. None of these grounds displaces the fee.

Driver's claims. The free-wait-served, arrival-corroborated, contact-met and fee-matches-policy points are accepted, as is the rider's own admission of lateness and her post-cancellation message. The claim about the missing advisory is not reinstated. The driver's separate discarded claim is not relied on.

No referral arises. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy amount, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show counter (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d) is not present on the profile, so that flag cannot be raised; and POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not apply because the driver attempted both message and call.

Confidence. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — trip record EV-TRIP-05051, GPS trace EV-GPS-05051, chat log EV-CHAT-05051 and fare ledger EV-FARE-05051 — is complete at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD first band, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final at any confidence, and neither party carries a fraud flag.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
